Commentary.Commentary: So 152 is the target for India. They might have started this game to try and chase down a target inside 10 or 15 overs, just so that their net run rate gets a good lift. But for now, they should be focusing on the win. Not on the type of the win. The players are back on the field. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana are the openers for India Women. Megan Schutt will start off to Shafali. Here we go.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

India will be happy with their bowling, but not their fielding. They dropped multiple catches and even though, individually, those did not matter match, but it certainly helped the partnerships grow. You never know, had those catches been taken at that point in time, Australia might have been kept to 130 or below. Barring Arundhati Reddy, who was slightly off colour, everyone bowled well, aiming to be wicket to wicket. Renuka Singh Thakur and Deepti Sharma picked up 2 wickets apiece.

Renuka Singh Thakur started a bit double-faced, struggling with the new ball to control her lines but then got 2 wickets in 2 balls. Australia then had a partnership through Grace Harris and Tahlia McGrath before a collapse saw them stutter from 79/2 to 101/5. But there was another rearguard action, this time from Ellyse Perry and Phoebe Litchfield, which helped them reach the 150-mark. Harris, McGrath and Perry batted really responsibly, not throwing it away, while the fact that we did not see a single half centurion shows how difficult it was, even for a set batter.

Not the traditional T20 matches where you see boundaries continuously. Australia batted at around 6-7 runs per throughout their innings but managed 50 runs in those last 5 overs, getting a bit of a lift. Just 2 sixes were hit in the overall innings, which tells you how difficult it was to clear the fence.

Well, eventually, after a big tussle throughout the innings, Australia Women have managed to touch the 150-mark. As per WV Raman's pitch analysis, 140 was a par score, but this does not look like a Bunsen pitch nor is it too slow. But yes, it is a competitive score for sure.

SIX! Phoebe Litchfield provides the perfect propulsion for Australia Women towards the backend with this huge six! Lands it full and in front of the stumps, Phoebe Litchfield sits down and slogs it over deep mid-wicket for a six.

Phoebe Litchfield alerts her but Jemimah Rodrigues is quick to make amends, gets up and picks the ball, and throws it to the bowler's end. Commentary.Commentary: LBW DECISION OVERTURNED! Well, we are talking so much about changes in ICC rules and regulations and this one is right up there for a debate. It was a tad shorter than full and Litchfield went for the reverse pull. She missed and was hit right in front of the stumps. Deepti appealed and the umpire, Sue Redfern, raised her finger. Litchfield had a chat with Perry and went for the review. UltraEdge indicates no bat or glove but Ball Tracker shows the ball to be PITCHING OUTSIDE LEG. Now, here is where controversy starts. The decision is reversed but the Indians are crowding around Redfern. Smriti Mandhana seems to indicate that if Litchfield played the switch hit, shouldn't the leg side now become an off side? The umpire seems to agree and sends it upstairs again. The third umpire has another look and determines that the position of the hands did not change while playing that shot and hence, it is not a switch hit, but a reverse sweep. So the decision is overturned once again. But the debate still remains - switch or reverse - shouldn't the angles change, if the batter changes the stance? Not just the grip? One for the lawkeepers.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. Engrossing three-quarters of an hour thus far. India have been up and about for this contest, eager to strike blows while Australia have been a tad cautious. Not sure whether that cautiousness is because of the wicket, where the ball is not quite coming onto the bat or is it simply because they lost two wickets pretty quickly. Considering the batting lineup they have, normally they go hard at the opposition bowlers but clearly, one can see that they feel they are up against a big challenge here. India have been largely unblemished, barring the initial new-ball spray from Renuka Singh Thakur where she conceded quite a few extras, but then she made up for it with her twin blows. Deepti Sharma would be eagerly hoping to either make up for that dropped chance of Grace Harris or see someone else dismiss her soon. Because if she hangs around, she can cause some damage. It is 50-50 at this stage, not quite sure who exactly is on top. Renuka Singh Thakur returns to bowl out. 3-0-19-2 so far.

Could have been a better effort in the field there! Deepti drags her length, around off, McGrath rocks back, cuts it to the right of diving Shafali Verma at cover-point but misses on the interception and deflects to her right. Harmanpreet Kaur scoots from cover, dives to her left and gets a hand to it. Commentary.Commentary: Okay! 'Advance Australia Fair' is done and so is 'Jana Gana Mana' and with that, we are all in readiness for a hopefully spicy contest to unfold. The Indians spread themselves out onto the field. They are now followed by the two Aussie openers - a new pair for this game - Beth Mooney and Grace Harris. Hard to say whether Harris just keeps smiling all the time or her face itself is so warm and friendly. Renuka Singh Thakur has the new ball in her hand. Normally, in Aus-Ind clashes, the Healy-Renuka contest is eagerly awaited. No Healy today, so Harris would be in the firing line. Here we go, the keeper is upto the stumps.
Time for the national anthems. It will be Australia's first, followed by India's.

Right then. How big is Healy's absence going to prove, for Australia? One does not need to be a rocket scientist to say that India have an early advantage even before this game gets going because to replace Healy, you need three players. You need a batter, who can take care of the opposition in the Powerplay and consistently score 50s and 100s in the semis and finals of a global tournament. Then, you need a keeper to be as quick as lightning with her glovework. And above all, you need someone who thinks ahead of the game at all times, as a captain. That's why her absence or presence is so critical to the Aussie team. But then, having said that, isn't the time ripe for the World Champions to prove that they are not a one-player unit? After their 2017 semifinal loss to India in the ODI World Cup, it was Meg Lanning's captaincy which took them to titles in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2023. So this is the first time in a long while that Australia will be without the services of one of their best ever captains. Do they have it in them to show to the world that it was a unit which won those titles and not just individual inspirations? We shall know soon.

PITCH REPORT - WV Raman is inspecting the surface. Observes that there is hardly any grass on it. Predicts that it will be drier and there will be turn for the spinners. Opines that the batters need to play sensible cricket and avoid big shots and playing across the line. But also feels that because one side of the ground is significantly shorter, a left-right combination could assist the batting team. Believes that 140 should be a par score on this wicket.

Indian captain, HARMANPREET KAUR, says that now India will aim to restrict Australia to a small total so that they can chase it down as quickly as possible. On India's plans for this game, Harman says that they have witnessed matches at this deck and have some plans which she hopes would be executed. On India being the last team to stop Australia's World Cup juggernaut in 2020, Kaur does not want to think about that for now and just wants to concentrate on playing good cricket. Informs that India have made one change, with Pooja Vastrakar coming in for Sajana Sajeevan.

Australian skipper, TAHLIA MCGRATH, says that they want to put some runs on the board and then try to defend the same. Feels lucky that they got to play a game at this venue before this clash and expects better adaptation from her team in this game. Understands that losing players in the middle of a big tournament is harmful but assures that the team is ready to deal with the situation with sufficient backups. Informs that Grace Harris and Darcie Brown come in for the injured Alyssa Healy and Tayla Vlaeminck tonight.

India Women (Playing XI) - Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Pooja Vastrakar (IN FOR SAJANA SAJEEVAN), Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil, Radha Yadav (IN FOR ASHA SOBHANA) and Renuka Singh Thakur.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Beth Mooney (WK), Grace Harris (IN FOR ALYSSA HEALY), Ellyse Perry, Ash Gardner, Phoebe Litchfield, Tahlia McGrath (C), Annabel Sutherland, Georgia Wareham, Sophie Molineux, Megan Schutt and Darcie Brown (IN PLACE OF TAYLA VLAEMINCK).
TOSS - Time for the flip of the coin. Tails is the call from McGrath and it is a tail. AUSTRALIA WILL BAT FIRST.
Back to Sharjah, we have got confirmed news - ALYSSA HEALY HAS BEEN RULED OUT OF TONIGHT'S CLASH. Tahlia McGrath will take over the reins with Ellyse Perry nominated as the vice captain.

Moving over to other international updates, from the region of Men's cricket, West Indies kick off their tour of Sri Lanka this evening. It is a plain white-ball tour, consisting of 3 T20Is and 3 ODIs. The T20Is would be played in Dambulla while the ODIs would be played in Pallekele. The first T20I was supposed to start by 1330 GMT but some rain before the game got the outfield damp, which delayed the toss. And from latest news, the drizzle has returned, so it might be a while before play starts in that region.

Earlier in the day, just before this clash, England trounced Scotland in the other group game in Sharjah itself. They chased down 110 in 10 overs - yes, just 10 overs - and what that's done is - propelled them to the top of the points table in Group B. Only one match remains in that group and it will be between West Indies and England. South Africa are done with their matches and are second for now, but should West Indies beat England on Tuesday, 15th October, by any minimum margin, it will be England and West Indies going through from Group B. If England win, it will be England and South Africa to make it through. But that still does not mean that England have qualified. If West Indies beat England by a huge margin on Tuesday, it could be West Indies and South Africa too!

Building on the previous update, we are getting news from Sharjah that Alyssa Healy was walking with the support of crutches. So that should definitely rule her out of tonight's clash, but assuming Australia's net run rate safely takes them through to the semis irrespective of what happens in this game and the New Zealand-Pakistan clash, would Healy be fit enough to play in the semifinal? From what we can see, one feels that the tournament is done for the knockout specialist. India have their own injury concern as well with Pooja Vastrakar undergoing a fitness test ahead of the game, with her right hamstring tightly strapped. Given the stakes of this clash, India would be tempted to play Vastrakar but at the same time, do they need to change the playing XI which performed so brilliantly against Sri Lanka?

Australia most probably will be without two of its stars today. Tayla Vlaeminck, their young pace sensation, took a tumble in their last outing and dislocated her shoulder, and has been ruled out of the tournament. Heather Graham has been called in the mix as her replacement. And skipper Alyssa Healy? She hobbled around with a foot injury. Will she play? Will she not? It's the million-dollar question running through every Aussie fans' minds. But we have seen this team having the luxury of bowling and batting options, in plentitude at their helm to cover any lapses.

But here's where it gets juicy, folks. For India, this isn't just another match - it's do or die. A win keeps their World Cup dreams alive, but a loss? Well, let's just say they'll be glued to their TV screens for the New Zealand-Pakistan game, praying for a miracle. So, the equation is simple yet oh-so-complicated - win, and win big, and dash the possibilities for others to roll over them.

Let's set the scene, shall we? Australia have been their usual dominant selves, steamrolling through Group A in their title defense with three wins from three. They already have one foot in the semifinal, but do not think for a second they'll be taking it easy. This is Australia we're talking about – they've got their eyes on a clean sweep - to make it 4 out of 4. After a stumble out of the gates against New Zealand, Indian ladies have roared back strongly. Two back-to-back wins, including a record-breaking triumph against Sri Lanka, have put them right back in contention.

In every major tournament, certain matchups generate buzz that eclipses the overall event hype. Fans eagerly await their favorite set of players to fight tooth and nail against each other. Welcome, cricket fans, to what promises to be an absolute cracker here at the historic Sharjah Cricket Ground! It's Match 18 of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2024, and we've got a marquee contest that's been circled on calendars worldwide. The defending champions, Australia Women, are set to lock horns with their fierce rivals, India Women. The buzz around this match has been electric, and for good reason!
... MATCH DAY ...

The 2024 Women's T20 World Cup is heating up as we approach the closing stages of the group phase. Aptly dubbed the 'Group of Death,' Group A has lived up to its reputation, with four out of five teams still in contention for a semifinal spot. In a highly anticipated rematch of the 2023 semifinal, India will face Australia at the iconic Sharjah Cricket Stadium, setting the stage for a high-stakes encounter. Australia are almost assured of a semifinal spot unless extreme results play out in the remaining Group A matches. A victory against India will seal their qualification, and even with a loss, they should be fine, provided it isn't by a big margin and New Zealand deliver a dominant win over Pakistan that swings the net run rate against them. So far, the defending champions have been in scintillating form, easily brushing aside their opponents and continuing their dominance in T20 World Cups. However, their joy from a recent victory over Pakistan was tempered by injury concerns around speedster Tayla Vlaeminck and captain Alyssa Healy. Vlaeminck, who dislocated her right shoulder while attempting to stop a boundary, has been ruled out of the tournament, with all-rounder Heather Graham named as her replacement. Healy sustained an acute foot injury, and her availability remains uncertain. Either Darcie Brown or Kim Garth could step in to fill the seamer role vacated by Vlaeminck. If Healy is unavailable, Grace Harris will likely be included in the lineup, with Tahlia McGrath expected to take over captaincy duties in Healy's absence. Australia have already played a couple of games at Sharjah, giving them a slight edge in understanding the conditions, while this will be India's first outing at the storied venue. Harmanpreet Kaur's side will need to adapt quickly in this crucial encounter. India had a shaky start to the tournament, with a heavy loss against New Zealand and a less-than-convincing win over Pakistan. However, they regained some lost ground with a dominant victory over Sri Lanka where their top order found form. Despite the resurgence, India’s path to the semifinals remains tricky. New Zealand's win over Sri Lanka has increased the pressure on Kaur and Co., meaning that even a win over Australia may not be enough to secure a semifinal spot. Although the Women in Blue currently have a better NRR, the White Ferns can overtake them, if they manage a comprehensive victory in their final group match against Pakistan. India who have only won one of their last five T20I encounters against Australia, face the daunting task of not just needing a win but needing to win big. Will they rise to the occasion? Or will Australia prove too strong once again? We shall find out.
